direct_answer: Shell states that its remuneration schemes are designed to support delivery of its corporate strategy and include structures intended to support reducing operational emissions and supporting customers to reduce their emissions [Source 1]. The majority of employees participate in an annual bonus scheme, while Executive Directors (and other nominated employees) receive long-term share awards [Source 1]. Shell indicates that its sustainability statement section on GOV-3 (and the Directors’ Remuneration Report) includes details of the sustainability-linked measures/targets/metrics used in performance assessment, the proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related performance, and the role of the Remuneration Committee in approving and updating the Directors’ Remuneration Policy [Source 1]. Shell also notes that performance and progress in the energy transition is measured against climate-related targets and ambition, including those reflected in the remuneration of senior management and employees, with a primary focus on reducing absolute GHG emissions and its Net Carbon Intensity (NCI) [Source 4].
